correctness.rationale: For every odd prime power, the lifting-the-exponent lemma gives \(\operatorname{ord}_{p^e}(2)=t_p p^{\max(0,e-h_p)}\). CRT and the least-common-multiple valuation give \(\nu_p(\ell(n))=\max(0,e_p-h_p,H_p)\), and LTE then gives \(\nu_p(2^{\ell(n)}-1)=\max(e_p,h_p+H_p)\). This proves both exact local quotient and gcd identities and both implications of the threshold theorem, including the boundary cases. The unit-cube argument yields the stated support-count error; standalone modular tests passed on 7,500 odd integers and six further supports, including exact nonzero valuation checks. Finite computations corroborate but do not prove the universal theorem.

value.rationale: Order-Wieferich numbers appear in a current asymptotic investigation, but the full local membership structure over arbitrary fixed prime supports is not characterized there. An exact one-minimum principal-upset classification and explicit gcd defect valuations cover all exponent vectors, distinguish cross-prime order obstructions from Wieferich heights, and yield a support-local asymptotic. This is a complete natural classification, not an arbitrary cutoff or a mere recomputation of OEIS entries. The proof is elementary, and global-density advances are not claimed.
